annotations.text:
Field-recording sheet — handoff §13.4.

Sized 794×1056: the A4/Letter intersection at 96 px/in, so one sheet prints correctly on either without shrink-to-fit.

Helvetica throughout, because the prefilled version is built by FPDF and FPDF has no other face — designing in a webfont would make the design and the shipped PDF disagree.

Pure black on white, and no grey: a dotted or 60%-grey rule is a sub-pixel mark that a 600 dpi mono engine halftones into a broken line or drops. The row heading band is a solid black bar with knocked-out text for the same reason.

The row-count sliders max out at what FITS. A slider that can silently cut the footer off the sheet is worse than no slider.

The three on the left are the deliverable: blank plant sheet, blank garden sheet, and the per-garden prefilled one FPDF generates.

The tick vocabulary is Carl\Domain\EventType's own labels, minus the ones set on the plant form or recorded automatically.

Every row is a flex row, not a CSS grid cell: a grid whose cells come out of a repeat needs every wrapper between it and them to be display:contents, and one that isn't turns nine columns into one.

Alternate direction, not the deliverable.

One row per observation, action written as a word instead of ticked: more lines per page, but it loses the tick-and-move-on speed of a watering round. Worth keeping on the canvas because the tradeoff is real — say if you'd rather have this one.
